messages:
veera: FYI customer acme-ai is seeing repeated 429s and allocation failures for their Dedicated pool in us-west-3. They reported timeouts and placement errors when creating new workers. Logs show 'placement failed: insufficient resources' and 'No available GPU capacity'.

jordan: got it, triaging. Is this affecting multiple tenants or just acme-ai?

veera: appears to be multi-tenant in the same AZ — two other dedicated customers reported slow API responses. acme-ai is the loudest though, escalated to support@.

michael: looking at scheduler, I can see placement rejects starting ~1971231000. Autoscaler didn't spin new instances because the placement pool is exhausted. Possible GPU stockout in us-west-3.

anya: can you paste the placement error blob? also any signs of noisy neighbor (OOMs, GPU throttling)?

veera: paste from acme logs: ```ERROR: placement failed: insufficient resources (requested: 16xA100, available: 0)
WARN: allocation retry loop triggered 5 times
REQUEST_ID=rc-87423```

jorge: customer reports they were on a reserved Dedicated plan. They expect failover to another region. Is cross-region failover automatic?

michael: not automatic for Dedicated by default. We have failover policies but customers must opt-in for cross-region routing. For now we can do an emergency manual failover to eu-west-1 if they accept changed latency.

anya: I'm seeing a surge of long-running noisy workloads from tenant id tenant-993 in the same pool — heavy 100k token generations keeping KV cache resident and blocking capacity. Suspect noisy neighbor.

jordan: can we throttle that tenant or move it to a lower-priority queue?

michael: we can apply an emergency QoS rule to deprioritize tenant-993 and drain its workers. Command I ran: `infractl qos set-priority --tenant tenant-993 --priority low --reason "emergency noisy-tenant"`

veera: customer asked for repro steps so their devs can confirm. Suggested steps I forwarded: 1) reproduce allocation with `POST /v1/dedicated/alloc` body {"gpus":16,"model":"gptx-8k"} 2) watch placement logs filter `placement.*insufficient` 3) capture `X-Request-Id`.

anya: policy note — if we trigger manual failover we need approval from SRE lead and billing (cross-region egress and reserved capacity differences). Jorge please confirm customer is happy with temporary billing delta.

jorge: acme-ai is ok with temporary failover and understands billing delta, they want action now. Approving manual failover.

michael: doing manual placement to eu-west-1 now. Command: `infractl place --region eu-west-1 --tenant acme-ai --force --size 16`

sre-bot: ALERT: dedicated-placement-failures-us-west-3 rate 87/min, affected-tenants: 4, autoscaler-disabled: false, timewindow: 10m

anya: after we place acme, keep throttling noisy tenant and schedule a postmortem to tune autoscaler thresholds and add a soft failover policy for reserved customers.

jordan: noted. I'll open an incident ticket for follow-up actions: autoscaler tuning, QoS knobs, and customer communication.

veera: thanks team — acme confirmed successful allocation in eu-west-1 and 429s stopped. Marking as mitigated, will follow up with full write-up and billing note. :white_check_mark:

michael: filing CAPEX note about increasing buffer for us-west-3.

anya: adding postmortem owners: anya, michael, jordan.

jorge: I'll send the customer summary and the temporary credits offer.

veera: closing thread for now, will update when PM/finance signs off on credits.
